bug_semantics: Apache Neethi policy normalization converts nested All/ExactlyOne (historically And/Xor) operators into DNF by taking an unbounded Cartesian cross-product of child alternatives. A crafted WS-Policy with N ExactlyOne children of two branches each produces 2^N All alternatives, allocating unbounded objects until the JVM heap is exhausted (CWE-400). The 3.2.2 patch adds MAX_ALTERNATIVES=10000 inside AbstractPolicyOperator.getCrossProduct and throws RuntimeException once the product exceeds that cap.
flaw_origin: The unbounded nested-loop Cartesian expansion was first written in the repository root commit that imported Policy.normalize from the pre-ASF scratch area. That method already combined every pair of child XorCompositeAssertion alternatives into new AndCompositeAssertion terms with no size bound. Later Neethi 2 work (AbstractPolicyOperator.crossProduct / getCrossProduct) is a rename/port of the same algorithm, not a new first-write.
